about: The lords of Xibalba send for the two brothers. Their messengers are four owls, Arrow Owl, One-Leg Owl, Macaw Owl and Head Owl, who come in an instant to the ball court where Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu are playing and deliver the summons word for word: come and play ball with us, and bring your gear and your rubber ball. The brothers go home to take leave of their mother Xmucane (their father is dead). They tie their ball up under the roof of the house, to be used again later, and charge Hunbatz and Hunchouen to keep to their flutes and songs, their writing and carving, and to keep the house and their grandmother's heart warm. Xmucane is overcome with grief; "we are not dying," they tell her. Led by the messengers they go down the steep road to Xibalba, through river gorges, through rushing water among countless trees, across a river of blood without drinking and across a river of water, until they reach a crossing of four roads, red, black, white and yellow. The black road speaks: "Take me, I am the lord's road." From there on they are beaten. In the council place of Xibalba they greet the first seated figures as Huncame and Vucub Came, but these are only an effigy and a carved wooden figure, and the lords roar with laughter. The brothers are asked to sit on the lords' bench, a burning-hot stone, and the lords laugh until they ache. Then the brothers are sent to the Dark House with a single lit torch and a lit cigar each, to be given back whole at dawn. They burn them up, and are defeated. The trials of Xibalba, the part ends, were many.

sentences.t: Catecut qui petic zamahel rumal Huncame, Vvcub Came:
sentences.l: Then their-coming messengers by Huncame, Vvcub Came:
sentences.i: Then the messengers came, sent by Huncame and Vucub Came:
sentences.n: The lords of Xibalba, who took counsel at the end of the last part, now send for the two brothers. qui petic 'their coming': qui- 'their' + pet 'come' + -ic, the verbal noun, standing as the verb of the sentence. zamahel 'messengers' (zamah 'errand' + agent -el) has no plural mark; the plural shows in qui 'their'. rumal 'by' names the senders. Huncame 'One Death' and Vvcub Came 'Seven Death' are the two highest lords of Xibalba; the English spells Vucub, as in 009.

sentences.t: “Quix bec, ix rahpop achih, he itaca ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.l: “You-go, you its-mat-lord of-men, go(?) you-summon the Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.i: “Go, you captains of the warriors, go and summon Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu.
sentences.n: The lords speak to their messengers. Quix bec 'go, you (pl.)': c- + ix 'you (pl.)' + be 'go' with -ec, the bec of earlier parts. rahpop achih (MS ixrahpopachih, divided by us; a title, printed in lower case like ahau): r- 'its' + ahpop, ah- 'he of' + pop 'mat', the woven mat on which lords sat in council (the pop of Popo Vuh), + achih 'man, warrior' (toggle achi). Brasseur's note calls it a title of the court of Xibalba, found long after at the K'iche' court, 'captain of the guards'; 'captains of the warriors' is built from him (inferred). he itaca (MS heitaca; Brasseur he y taka): the i is taken as i- 'you (pl.)' and joined to the verb, taca from taq 'send, send for' (009's tacoc; toggle itaqa), so 'you summon'. he is taken as a form of the verb 'go' (Ho na 'we go now' in ¶6, hix 'go, you (pl.)' in ¶15). Brasseur's note makes he stand for ho-e, the third person plural ('that they go'), though his French has 'allez, vous'; whose 'go' it is is not clear (inferred; toggle je by the letters).

sentences.t: Quix ꜭha ta: Quix opon cuꜭ.
sentences.l: You-say (ta): You-arrive-there with-us.
sentences.i: Tell them: Come to us.
sentences.n: Quix ꜭha ta 'say (it), you (pl.)': ꜭh is the colonial letter for ch', and ꜭha 'say' is the word that closes speeches; ta softens the command. Quix opon cuꜭ 'you shall arrive there with us': opon is to arrive at a place away from the speaker (vl is to arrive here): the words are framed for the messengers to say at the ball court, of a journey there, to Xibalba, while the lords' own wish in the next lines uses vl 'come here' (inferred). cuꜭ is 'with them' or 'with us' by the same letters; here Brasseur has kuq 'with us', and the toggle gives quk' (q- 'our' + uꜭ 'company').

sentences.t: Que petoc, que ꜭha ahauab chivech.
sentences.l: They-come, they-say lords to-you.
sentences.i: ‘Let them come,’ say the lords to you.
sentences.n: The message the brothers are to hear, in the lords' own voice. Que petoc 'let them come': que is c- + e 'they', petoc is pet 'come' + -oc, as in 007. que ꜭha 'they say'. ahauab 'lords' (ahau + plural -ab). chivech 'to you (pl.)': chi + iv- 'your (pl.)' + ech.

sentences.t: Varal tah que vl chaaha vi cuꜭ;
sentences.l: Here may they come-here play there with-us;
sentences.i: Let them come here and play with us;
sentences.n: tah is the particle of wishing: 'here may they …'. que vl 'they come here': vl 'arrive here', the counterpart of opon. chaaha 'play (ball)': the chaah of the last part with -a (inferred; toggle chaaja, as chaaj). vi points back to varal 'here'. cuꜭ 'with us' (Brasseur kuq). In the manuscript a blot follows a cuꜭ at the end of a line in this passage (image 0035, line 36); nothing was read in it.

sentences.t: chi ca caztah ta ca vach cuꜭ.
sentences.l: that ca come-alive (ta) our face with-them.
sentences.i: so that our faces may come alive with them.
sentences.n: caztah: Brasseur reads qaztah (his q is ꜭ), 'that we may enliven our faces'. It is taken as ꜭaz 'live', the root of ꜭazlem 'life' in the first part, + -tah 'become', 'come alive, revive'; the toggle restores k' (k'astaj) because the root is known (inferred). To make the face come alive is taken as to be cheered, to have sport (inferred). The first ca is left unexplained (perhaps the ongoing c-, toggle ka; Brasseur prints ka for both, his k standing for q, as if ca- 'we' twice); the second is ca- 'our'. This cuꜭ is read 'with them', with Brasseur's cuq (toggle kuk'); the line before has the same letters as 'with us'.

sentences.t: Quiꜩih ca ca maihah qui chi.
sentences.l: Truly ca we-marvel-at their mouth.
sentences.i: Truly, we marvel at their mouths.
sentences.n: MS qui|ꜩih cacamaihah, divided with Brasseur (quitzih ca ka maihah). quiꜩih 'truly'. ca ca: the ongoing c- written ca (toggle ka), then ca- 'we' (toggle qa); Brasseur's note: 'ca ka maihah qui chi, we admire their mouths'. maihah 'marvel at', as in an earlier part (inferred). qui chi 'their mouths' (chi 'mouth', toggle chi'): what comes out of them, the shouting of the game that vexed the lords in the last part. The marvelling is perhaps ironic (inferred).

sentences.t: Quehecut que pe vi, que ꜭha ahauab.
sentences.l: Thus-then they come there, they-say lords.
sentences.i: So let them come, say the lords.
sentences.n: Quehecut 'so then': quehe 'thus' + cut 'then' written as one word (toggle Keje'k'ut, as in 008). que pe vi 'let them come (there)': pe 'come', vi pointing to the place. que ꜭha ahauab 'say the lords' closes each part of the message, as a herald would.

sentences.t: Chi qui cam cu vloc ri qui choconizan, qui bate, qui pachcab; chi pe naipuch ri qui quic, que ꜭha ahauab.
sentences.l: Let they-take then hither the their implements, their rings(?), their hand-guards(?); let come likewise the their rubber, they-say lords.
sentences.i: Let them bring their gear, their rings, their hand-guards; and let their rubber ball come too, say the lords.
sentences.n: A couplet: chi qui cam … vloc 'let them take … hither', that is, bring, and chi pe 'let (it) come'. cam 'take' (toggle k'am; Brasseur qam). choconizan: chocon 'serve, be of use' (the choconic of an earlier part) + -iza 'make' + -n, 'what they use', their gear (inferred; Brasseur turns it into 'the instruments with which they make all that noise'). bate and pachcab are the rings and hand-guards of the last part (guesses after Brasseur's 'anneaux', 'gants'). naipuch 'likewise also': nai + puch, written as one word (toggle naypuch, as nai is nay). quic is the word for blood and also for rubber, here the rubber ball (Brasseur 'their balls of elastic gum'); toggle kik', the known word. In the manuscript the letters of qui quic are crowded (quiquiqque); quic is read as in the last part and as the clear ca quic of ¶6, a doubtful reading.

sentences.t: Quix ꜭha ta: Quix oponoc,” xe vꜭhaxic ri zamahel.
sentences.l: You-say (ta): You-arrive-there,” they-were-told the messengers.
sentences.i: Tell them: Come,” the messengers were told.
sentences.n: The lords' speech ends as it began, with Quix ꜭha ta 'tell them'. oponoc: opon 'arrive there' + -oc, as petoc. xe vꜭhaxic 'they were told': xe- 'they' + vꜭhaxic, ꜭha 'speak' with passive -x- + -ic.

sentences.t: Are cut qui zamahel ri Tucur: Chabi Tucur, Huracan Tucur, Caquix Tucur, Holom Tucur, que vꜭhaxic v zamahel Xibalba.
sentences.l: This then their messengers the Owl: Arrow Owl, One-Leg Owl, Macaw Owl, Head Owl, thus they-are-called its messengers Xibalba.
sentences.i: Their messengers were the owls: Arrow Owl, One-Leg Owl, Macaw Owl and Head Owl, as the messengers of Xibalba are called.
sentences.n: tucur is the owl (Brasseur 'hibou'; toggle tukur), singular for the kind. The four names describe the birds, and the next two sentences explain each, so they are translated as epithets, while the toggle keeps the K'iche'. Chabi Tucur: chab + -i, chab read 'arrow' with Brasseur (his note on cha at the torch, ¶17: cha is the word, the arrow, and the arrow point; his French 'Flèche-de-Hibou'), inferred. Huracan Tucur: the text itself reads the name as hun racan 'one leg' (next sentence); it is the same name as Huracan, the Heart of Sky, which stays untranslated where it is his name. Caquix Tucur: caquix is the macaw of Vvcub Caquix. Holom Tucur: holom 'head'. Brasseur's note thinks the owls are named from Tucurub, a town in the Verapaz; that is his guess. que vꜭhaxic 'as they are called'.

sentences.t: Are ri Chabi Tucur queheri chab, xa copquic; are curi Huracan Tucur, xa hun racan ꜭo vxic.
sentences.l: This the Arrow Owl like arrow, only copquic(?); this then One-Leg Owl, only one its-leg there-is its-wings(?).
sentences.i: Arrow Owl was like an arrow, swift (?); One-Leg Owl had only one leg, and wings.
sentences.n: queheri 'like, as'. chab is read 'arrow' with Brasseur, who renders 'as swift as an arrow'; copquic is not otherwise known, and 'swift' is his (a guess; toggle by the letters). xa hun racan 'only one leg': racan 'his leg' (r- + acan), so hun racan explains the name Huracan. ꜭo vxic 'there are its wings': ꜭo 'there is' + vxic, here taken as v- 'its' + xic 'wing' (modern xik'), the sense Brasseur gives it for Head Owl below ('mais des ailes'); for this owl and the next he renders 'its nature was'. In earlier parts vxic was 'becoming', and 'wing' was raised there as possible; the toggle keeps uxik (inferred).

sentences.t: Are curi Caquix Tucur, caꜫ rih ꜭo vxic; are chi naipuch ri Holom Tucur, xa vtuquel vholom, ma habi racan, xa vxic ꜭolic.
sentences.l: This then Macaw Owl, red(?) its-back, there-is its-wings(?); this again likewise the Head Owl, only alone its-head, not there-is its-leg, only its-wings(?) being-there.
sentences.i: Macaw Owl had a red (?) back, and wings; and Head Owl was only a head: it had no legs, only wings.
sentences.n: caꜫ rih 'red (?) its back': rih 'its back' (r- + ih). caꜫ is written with c and the tresillo; Brasseur reads gag, the word for fire, and renders 'its nature was of fire all around'. The macaw is red, and 'red' is inferred; the toggle respells the letters (kaq'; the modern word for red is kaq). are chi naipuch 'this, again likewise': chi is chic with its c shared (toggle chik). Head Owl is xa vtuquel vholom 'only its head by itself', ma habi racan 'it has no legs', xa vxic ꜭolic 'only wings were there' (ꜭolic 'being there', the positional); here Brasseur too has 'wings'.

sentences.t: E cahib ri zamahel, rahpop achihab.
sentences.l: They four the messengers, its-mat-lords of-men.
sentences.i: The messengers were four, captains of the warriors.
sentences.n: E cahib 'they (were) four': e, the plural, before the numeral, as e caib in the last part. rahpop achihab: the title of ¶1 with the plural -ab on achih 'man' (toggle achijab').

sentences.t: Que calem ta xe pe cut chila chi Xibalba; libah chi xe vlic, e cu tacal chuvi hom.
sentences.l: They calem(?) when they-came then there from Xibalba; instantly they-arrived-here, they then alighted on-top ball-court.
sentences.i: They came from there, from Xibalba, and in an instant they had arrived and alighted on the ball court.
sentences.n: Que calem is a doubtful reading (MS quecalem taxepecut): the third letter is a tall looped l, and Brasseur's OCR is garbled here; his French has 'setting out from Xibalba'. que may be c- + e 'they'; calem is not otherwise known and is left out of the English (toggle by the letters). chila chi Xibalba 'there, at Xibalba'. libah chi 'in an instant' is 009's libahchi, written apart here (toggle lib'aj chi). xe vlic 'they arrived here': vl + -ic, the ending at the end of a clause. e cu tacal 'they alighted': tacal as in earlier parts (inferred), said of a bird coming to rest. chuvi hom 'on top of the ball court'.

sentences.t: Que chaah cut Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu pa hom ri Nim Xob Carchah chuꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: They-play then Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu in ball-court the Nim Xob Carchah it-is-called.
sentences.i: Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu were playing ball in the court called Nim Xob Carchah.
sentences.n: que chaah 'they are playing': c- (ongoing) + e 'they' + chaah 'play (ball)'. Nim Xob Carchah (divided by us) is kept as a place name: nim 'great' and xob 'fear', as in the last part (Brasseur 'the Great Affront of Carchah'). Carchah is, Brasseur says, a large Indian town near Cobán in the Verapaz; he takes the name as 'fish of ash'. chuꜭhaxic 'as it is called'.

sentences.t: E cu tacatoh ri Tucur chuvi hom ta xqui zac cut qui ꜩih;
sentences.l: They then sent(?) the Owl on-top ball-court when they-made-clear then their word;
sentences.i: The owls sent to the ball court then spoke their message plainly,
sentences.n: tacatoh is not otherwise known; Brasseur reads takatoh and renders 'the owls sent (to the ball court)', from tac 'send' (the taca of ¶1); inferred, toggle taqatoj, as 009's taqoq. xqui zac 'they made clear': zac 'white, clear' used as a verb, 'they spoke out' (inferred; Brasseur 'délivrèrent leur message'). Here the manuscript has the plain z (zac); four manuscript lines on (the sentence after next) it writes Xꜩac qui ꜩih with the tz ligature. Each is printed as written and read as a different word.

sentences.t: xavi xere vcholic vꜩih Huncame, Vvcub Came, Ahalpuh, Ahalcana, Chamiabac, Chamiaholom, Xiquiripat, Cuchumaquic, Ahalmez, Ahaltocob, Xic, Patan, qui bi conohel ahauab.
sentences.l: just thus its-ordering its-word Huncame, Vvcub Came, Ahalpuh, Ahalcana, Chamiabac, Chamiaholom, Xiquiripat, Cuchumaquic, Ahalmez, Ahaltocob, Xic, Patan, their name all lords.
sentences.i: word for word as Huncame and Vucub Came, Ahalpuh and Ahalq'ana, Chamiabac and Chamiaholom, Xiquiripat and Cuchumaquic, Ahalmez and Ahaltocob, Xic and Patan had set it out: those were the names of all the lords.
sentences.n: xavi xere 'just so, exactly'. vcholic: v- 'its' + chol 'set in a row, in order' + -ic (inferred, after Brasseur 'in the same order of speech'); vꜩih 'its word'. The owls repeat the message as all the lords framed it. The lords are those named in the last part, here in another order. Ahalcana is written here with plain c (clear in the MS), where 009 printed Ahalꜫana with the tresillo; Brasseur has Ahalgana in both places. The toggle and the English keep 009's form for the same lord (Ajalq'ana, Ahalq'ana). qui bi conohel ahauab 'the names of all the lords'.

sentences.t: Xꜩac qui ꜩih cumal Tucur.
sentences.l: It-fell their word by Owl.
sentences.i: So the owls let the lords' word fall.
sentences.n: Xꜩac 'it fell, dropped' (with the tz ligature; compare xqui zac above). With cumal 'by them' the sentence reads 'their word was let fall by the owls', that is, delivered (inferred; Brasseur turns it the other way: the lords had arranged their word for the owls). qui ꜩih 'their word', the lords'.

sentences.t: “Ma quiꜩih ca ꜭha ahau Huncame, Vvcub Came?”
sentences.l: “(Is it) not truly he-says lord Huncame, Vvcub Came?”
sentences.i: “Is it true that the lord Huncame and Vucub Came say this?”
sentences.n: The brothers answer the owls. Ma marks the question ('is it not …?'). ca ꜭha 'he says': ca, the ongoing c-, + ꜭha 'say'. ahau 'lord' stands singular before the pair, as vbi ahau did in the last part.

sentences.t: “Quiꜩih bala,” que ꜭha.
sentences.l: “Truly indeed,” they-say.
sentences.i: “It is true indeed,” they say.
sentences.n: bala strengthens what goes before it, as in Vꜩ bala 'very well' (inferred, as in earlier parts). que ꜭha 'they say': the owls.

sentences.t: “Oh na cu achbilai ive?”
sentences.l: “We then (cu) go-along-with(?) you?”
sentences.i: “And are we to go with you?”
sentences.n: Oh 'we'. achbilai: ach 'companion', the root of rach 'together with' and of the achbilan 'going along with' of an earlier part, + -bil + -ai (inferred). ive 'you (pl.)', the ive of chive 'to you'. Brasseur: 'is it really true that we must go with you?'

sentences.t: “Chi cam vloc ri ronohel queꜩabal, que ꜭha ahauab.”
sentences.l: “Let-take hither the all their-play-gear, they-say lords.”
sentences.i: “Let them bring all their gear for the game, say the lords.”
sentences.n: The owls answer with the lords' words. Chi cam vloc 'let (them) bring': chi + cam 'take' + vloc 'hither'; no person is written, and 'them' is from the sense. queꜩabal 'their gear for play', as in the last part (toggle ketz'ab'al, inferred).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; coh iuoiobeh na.
sentences.l: “Good bala; us you-wait-for first.
sentences.i: “Very well; wait for us a moment.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well', as in the house table. coh iuoiobeh 'you wait for us' (MS cohiuoiobeh; Brasseur koh vv'oyobeh): coh, c- + oh 'us', the object; iu-, iv- 'you (pl.)' before a vowel; oiob 'wait' with -eh, the ending of a transitive verb (inferred). The u and i are printed as the manuscript has them; toggle iwoyob'ej. na 'first, for now'.

sentences.t: Oh na ca pixabah can na ca chuch,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: We first we-charge behind first our mother,” they-said then.
sentences.i: We must first take leave of our mother,” they said.
sentences.n: ca pixabah can 'we leave word with': ca- 'we' + pixabah 'charge, counsel' (the pixab of pixabaxic in ¶6) + can 'behind', the root of canah 'remain', so 'leave a charge behind' (inferred; Brasseur 'take leave of our mother'). ca chuch 'our mother' is Xmucane. na 'first' comes twice.

sentences.t: Xe be cut chi cochoch, xeꜭha cut chire qui chuch (xcaminac oc qui cahau):
sentences.l: They-went then to their-home, they-said then to-her their mother (he-had-died already their father):
sentences.i: So they went to their home, and said to their mother (their father had already died):
sentences.n: chi cochoch 'to their home': c- 'their' (qui- before a vowel) + ochoch 'home'. chire 'to her'. The brackets are ours. xcaminac oc 'he had already died', as was said of the boys' own mother in the last part: their father Xpiyacoc is dead, and only their mother Xmucane, the grandmother of Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen, is left.

sentences.t: “Ho na, ix ca chuch; xa et culic.
sentences.l: “We-go now, you our mother; only et(?) culic(?).
sentences.i: “We are going now, our mother; but it is for nothing (?).
sentences.n: Ho na 'we go now': ho is the verb 'go', here for 'we' (inferred); Brasseur's note at ¶1 names the verb Ho 'aller' and gives hin 'that I go' (ho-in) and he 'that they go' (ho-e); toggle jo, by the letters. ix ca chuch 'you, our mother'. xa et culic (Brasseur xaet k'ulic) is not understood. Brasseur renders 'but our journey will be in vain', and 'for nothing' is a guess from him. et may be the et of vetal 'its sign', and culic may be c- + vl 'arrive' + -ic; Brasseur's division k'ulic, his k standing for q, would make it q- 'our' + vl + -ic, 'our arrival', which suits his 'our journey' (inferred). The toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: Mi xul v zamahel ahau, camol que.
sentences.l: Just it-arrived its messenger(s) lord, taker(s) of-us.
sentences.i: The lord's messengers have just come to take us.
sentences.n: Mi 'just now' before a completed verb: mi xul 'has just arrived'. camol 'taker': cam 'take' + -ol, the agent ending (Brasseur qamol; toggle k'amol). que is here 'us' (Brasseur 'to take us'); the toggle gives qe.

sentences.t: Que pe toc, ca ꜭha cut, que ꜭha tacol que.
sentences.l: They come (-toc), he-says then, they-say summoners of-us.
sentences.i: ‘Let them come,’ he says; so say those sent to summon us.
sentences.n: Que pe toc: the petoc 'let them come' of the message, here written as two words. ca ꜭha 'he says', the lord; que ꜭha 'they say', the messengers. tacol 'summoner, one who sends for': tac 'send' + -ol (toggle taqol, as itaca itaqa in ¶1). que 'us' (toggle qe).

sentences.t: Xchi canah cu cana va ca quic,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: It-shall-remain then remaining this our rubber,” they-said then.
sentences.i: This ball of ours will stay behind,” they said.
sentences.n: Xchi canah 'it shall remain': xchi- 'shall' + canah 'remain'. cana is taken as the same root again, 'left behind', as Xe canah cu canoc 'they stayed, left behind' in the last part (inferred); Brasseur reads gana and makes the ball 'a witness (of our existence)'. va ca quic 'this our rubber', the ball (toggle kik'); here the word is clear in the manuscript.

sentences.t: Cate xbe qui xima can oc pu vi ha ꜭohul.
sentences.l: Then went they tied-it behind (oc) in-its top house there-is-hollow.
sentences.i: Then they went and tied it up under the roof of the house, in a hollow there.
sentences.n: xbe qui xima 'they went and tied it': x- + be 'go', then qui- 'they' + xim 'tie, bind' + -a (inferred; Brasseur 'they went to hang it up'). can oc 'leaving it': can 'behind' with the ending oc of direction. pu vi ha 'in the top of the house': pu is pa 'in' + v- 'its', contracted (Brasseur's note at ¶8: pu for pa u, p'u 'in the'; the glossary's pu chi' 'in the mouth'), vi 'head, top' (toggle wi'), ha 'house' (toggle ja). ꜭohul is ꜭo 'there is' + hul 'hollow' written as one word (Brasseur qo hul): 'where there is a hollow'. The division qui xima can oc pu vi is ours.

sentences.t: “Na cate chi ca choconizah chic.
sentences.l: “Not-until then shall we-use-it again.
sentences.i: “Not until later shall we use it again.
sentences.n: Na cate 'not until then, only later'. chi ca choconizah 'we shall use it': chi + ca- 'we' + choconizah, the verb of choconizan in ¶1 (chocon 'be of use' + -iza 'make' + -h; inferred). Brasseur: 'we shall play ball again'.

sentences.t: Xa quix ꜩuan oc, xa pu quix bixan oc, quix ziban oc, quix coton oc;
sentences.l: Only you-make-music (oc), only also you-sing (oc), you-write (oc), you-carve (oc);
sentences.i: You are only to make music and sing, to write and paint, and to carve;
sentences.n: The fathers charge their sons with the arts of the last part. quix … oc 'you (pl.) shall keep on …', four verbs in -an (coton in -on), the ending of an action with no object: ꜩuan 'make music' (Brasseur tzuan, 'faites de la musique'; perhaps the zu 'flute' of ahzu, though written with the tz ligature; inferred), bixan 'sing' (bix 'song'), ziban 'write, paint', coton 'carve' (cot, as in ahcot; Brasseur goton; toggle koton, as ajkot). ziban is presumably the ꜩib 'write, paint' of ahꜩibenai, but the manuscript here has the plain z (Brasseur's OCR triban); it is printed as written, and the toggle respells the letters (sib'an).

sentences.t: chi mecoh cochoch, chi mecoh puch iꜭux ivatit,” xe vꜭhax cut Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen ta xe pixabaxic.
sentences.l: let-it-be-warm our-home, let-it-be-warm also your-heart your-grandmother,” were-told then Hunbaꜩ, Hunchouen when they-were-charged.
sentences.i: keep our home warm, and keep warm the heart of your grandmother,” Hunbatz and Hunchouen were told when they were given their charge.
sentences.n: A couplet: chi mecoh … chi mecoh 'let it be warm … let it be warm'. mecoh is read with Brasseur (megoh, his g is ꜫ; 'réchauffez') and the modern word meq' 'warm', so the toggle restores q' (inferred). cochoch is here 'our home': c- for ca- 'our' before a vowel (toggle qochoch; Brasseur too writes k'ochoch here, his k standing for q, against c'ochoch 'their home' at the start of the paragraph), where at the start of the paragraph the same letters were 'their home'. iꜭux ivatit 'your heart, your grandmother': the manuscript has i- 'your (pl.)' on both words (Brasseur u qux vv'atit; his French 'le cœur de votre aïeule'); read as 'the heart of your grandmother' (inferred). The q-shaped letter of iꜭux is read ꜭ, as in the last part. Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen are Hunhunahpu's sons (toggle Junb'atz', as in 009).

sentences.t: Quzquz cut choc qui chuch ri Xmucane.
sentences.l: Quzquz(?) then it-enters their mother the Xmucane.
sentences.i: Then grief came over their mother Xmucane.
sentences.n: quzquz is not otherwise known; Brasseur reads guzguz (his g is ꜫ) and renders 'emotion overcame Xmucane, and she wept'. choc 'it enters' (ch- + oc 'enter'), so 'quzquz entered their mother'. 'Grief' is a guess; the toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: “Ho na; ma habi coh camic, mi xbizonic,” xeꜭha ta xe bec Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.l: “We-go now; not there-is we-die, do-not(?) grieve,” they-said when they-went Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.i: “We are going now; we are not dying. Do not grieve,” said Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu as they went.
sentences.n: ma habi coh camic 'it is not that we die': coh, c- + oh 'we', + camic 'die'. mi xbizonic (MS mi|xbizonic; Brasseur m'vx bizonic): bizon 'grieve, worry' (the bizonic of an earlier part) + -ic. The sense 'do not grieve' is Brasseur's and fits; the form is not clear, since mi elsewhere is 'just now', and the x may stand for ix 'you (pl.)' (inferred). xe bec 'they went' (be + -ec).

sentences.t: Cate puch ta xe bec Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu, xcam qui be cumal ri zamahel.
sentences.l: Then also when they-went Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu, it-was-taken their road by the messengers.
sentences.i: And when Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu set out, the messengers led them on their way.
sentences.n: A new paragraph in the manuscript. xcam qui be cumal 'their road was taken by them': cam 'take' (toggle k'am; Brasseur qam), here with cumal 'by them', so passive in sense. The messengers took the road ahead of them, that is, led the way (Brasseur 'took the road before them').

sentences.t: Ta xe cah cut pu beal Xibalba, xuluxuh vchi cumuc.
sentences.l: Then they-went-down then in-its road Xibalba, xuluxuh(?) its-mouth cumuc(?).
sentences.i: Then they went down by the road to Xibalba, where the way fell steeply (?).
sentences.n: xe cah 'they went down': cah is the verb 'go down' (toggle qaj, as cahic qajik in the glossary), not cah 'sky'. pu beal 'by the road': pu is pa 'in' + v- 'its', contracted (Brasseur's note: pu for pa u, p'u 'in the'), beal 'road' (be + -al). xuluxuh vchi cumuc is not understood. Brasseur's French has the first stages of the descent 'very steep'. xuluxuh may be a doubled xul (perhaps 'go down'), vchi is 'its mouth, its edge', and cumuc is not otherwise known (Brasseur cumuk). The English is a guess from Brasseur; the toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: Xe cah cut ta xe el chi cu apon oc chu chi hal ha zivanub, Nuzivan Cul, Cuzivan v bi.
sentences.l: They-went-down then when they-came-out, again then arriving (oc) at-its mouth changing(?) water ravines, Nuzivan Cul, Cuzivan its name.
sentences.i: Down they went, and they came out and reached the edge of a rushing river (?) in the ravines, the ones called Nuzivan Cul and Cuzivan.
sentences.n: chi cu: chic 'again' with its c shared with cu (toggle chik k'u). chu chi 'at its mouth, its edge' (chi 'mouth', toggle chi'). hal ha: hal 'change' + ha 'water' (toggle ja'), taken as a moving, rushing river (inferred; Brasseur 'a rapid river', his text hal-hàc). zivanub: zivan 'ravine, gorge' + -ub, not otherwise known (perhaps a plural). Nuzivan Cul and Cuzivan (MS nuzivan cul, cuzivan) are kept as the names of the gorges; Brasseur gives nu zivan cul 'my ravine of throat' and cu zivan 'gorge-ravine', for their depth and narrow windings (inferred). v bi 'its name', written apart.

sentences.t: Xe eco vi; xe eco chi cut chupan halhal ha zimah; maui ahilan zimah.
sentences.l: They-crossed there; they-crossed again then within churning(?) water zimah(?); not counted zimah(?).
sentences.i: They crossed there; and again they crossed, through churning water among calabash trees (?), calabash trees past counting.
sentences.n: eco 'pass, cross' (Brasseur eqo, his q standing for ꜭ, 'they passed'; for icou he writes iqo, iqou), taken as the verb of an earlier part's ecouic and of icou below (ik'ow); the toggle respells the letters (eko). chi cut: chic with its c shared (toggle chik k'ut). halhal ha: hal doubled, 'churning, rushing water' (Brasseur 'eaux bouillonnantes'; inferred). zimah is read with Brasseur as calabash trees (he also renders a later king's name, Cavizimah, 'calebassier orné ou armé', adorned or armed calabash tree); a guess, and the toggle respells the letters. maui ahilan 'not counted' (ahilan, as in an earlier part).

sentences.t: Xe icou vi, maui xe tocotahic.
sentences.l: They-passed there, not they-were-tocot-ed(?).
sentences.i: They passed through, and were not hurt (?).
sentences.n: icou 'pass' (toggle ik'ow, as in earlier parts). tocotahic: tocot + passive -ah + -ic; Brasseur reads togotahic, 'without hurting themselves'. 'Hurt' (perhaps 'pierced') is a guess; the root may be that of 009's tocota 'strike down' (a guess there too). Toggle by the letters.

sentences.t: Ta xe opon chicut chi a, chi quiqui a; xe icou chiri, maui xcucah.
sentences.l: Then they-arrived again-then at river, at blood river; they-crossed there, not they-drank.
sentences.i: Then they came to a river, a river of blood; they crossed it, and did not drink.
sentences.n: chi a, chi quiqui a 'at a river, at a river of blood' (MS chi a | chi qui qui a): a 'river' is read with Brasseur's chi quiqi-a 'at the river of blood'. The first word is a, where Brasseur has u, and quiqui is joined as one word, quic 'blood' + -i (toggle kik'i); both are doubtful readings. xcucah 'they drank': x- + c- (qui- 'they' before a vowel) + ucah 'drink' (Brasseur x-c'uqah, 'without drinking'; toggle xkuk'aj, as cucah quk'aj 'we drink' in an earlier part).

sentences.t: Xe opon chi a vtuquel puch chi a, maui xe chacatahic.
sentences.l: They-arrived at river, alone also at river, not they-were-brought-low.
sentences.i: They came to a river, a river of water only, and they were not brought low.
sentences.n: vtuquel 'by itself, alone': a river that was only river, of water alone (Brasseur 'another river, but with only water'; inferred). maui xe chacatahic 'they were not brought low': Xibalba has not yet caught them (Brasseur: 'they had not been taken in any ambush').

sentences.t: Xavi xe icou chic, ta xe opon chicut pa cahib xalcat be;
sentences.l: Also they-crossed again, then they-arrived again-then at four crossing(?) road;
sentences.i: They crossed this one too, and then they came to a crossing of four roads;
sentences.n: xalcat is taken as 'crossing, fork' with Brasseur ('where four roads met'): pa cahib xalcat be 'at the four crossing roads', a crossroads (inferred; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: ca chiri cut xe chacatah vi pa cahib xalcat be: hun ꜫaꜫa be, hun cut queca be, zaqui be hun, hun cut ꜫana be, cahib be.
sentences.l: ca there then they-were-brought-low there at four crossing road: one red road, one then black road, white road one, one then yellow road, four roads.
sentences.i: and there, at the crossing of four roads, they were brought low: one road red, one black, one white, one yellow, four roads.
sentences.n: ca is left unrendered, as in earlier parts. xe chacatah vi 'they were brought low there' (chacatah, the word of Vucub Caquix's downfall). The four roads: ꜫaꜫa 'red' (two tresillos in the MS; Brasseur caka, 'rouge'); the modern word is kaq, so the toggle only respells the letters (q'aq'a). queca 'black': plain c, Brasseur geka; it is queꜫ, the root of queꜫum 'darkness', so the toggle restores q'eqa. zaqui 'white'; ꜫana 'yellow', the ꜫana of the last part. ꜫaꜫa, queca and ꜫana take -a, zaqui -i. zaqui be hun 'white road one' turns the pattern round.

sentences.t: Are cut xꜭhau ri queca be: “In quinicamo, in vbe ahau,” xꜭhau ri be.
sentences.l: This then it-spoke the black road: “I, you-take-me, I its-road lord,” it-spoke the road.
sentences.i: And the black road spoke: “Take me: I am the lord's road,” said the road.
sentences.n: xꜭhau 'it spoke' (ꜭhau 'speak'). quinicamo, one word here (Brasseur quin y qamo): c- (ongoing) + in 'me' + i- 'you (pl.)' + cam 'take' + -o, 'you take me' (toggle kinik'amo). in vbe ahau 'I (am) the lord's road': the second in has a tail and could be read ir; it is taken as in, with Brasseur. Brasseur's note: in Ximénez's version the road itself speaks; he thinks it is the road's guardian.

sentences.t: Chiri cut xe ꜭhacatah vi.
sentences.l: There then they-were-brought-low there.
sentences.i: There they were brought low.
sentences.n: Here only the manuscript writes the verb with gh, ꜭhacatah (MS xeghacatah vi, image 0037 line 31), where its four other occurrences in this part are chacatah(ic) with plain ch; Brasseur has chakatah. It is printed as written, a doubtful reading, and the toggle respells the letters (ch'akataj). It may be the verb of 009's chac 'defeat' (modern ch'ak 'win'), which would make ꜭh the better spelling; that is not certain.

sentences.t: Are xqui taqueh ri be Xibalba, ta xe opon cut pa qui popobal rahaual Xibalba; xe chacatah chicut chiri.
sentences.l: This they-followed the road Xibalba, when they-arrived then at their council-place its-lords Xibalba; they-were-brought-low again-then there.
sentences.i: They followed the road to Xibalba, and when they came to the council place of the lords of Xibalba, they were brought low there again.
sentences.n: xqui taqueh 'they followed' (Brasseur takeh), taken as the taquen 'keep on, follow' of an earlier part (inferred; toggle taqej). popobal 'council place': pop 'mat' + -obal, the place of the mat where lords sat (Brasseur 'the hall where the kings of Xibalba sat enthroned'). rahaual Xibalba 'the lords of Xibalba'.

sentences.t: Are nabe cubulel ri xa poy, xa aham che, cautalic cumal Xibalba.
sentences.l: This first seated-ones the only effigy, only carved wood, set-up(?) by Xibalba.
sentences.i: The first ones seated there were only an effigy, only a figure of carved wood, set up by Xibalba.
sentences.n: cubulel 'seated ones': cubul 'seated', a positional, + -el. poy 'effigy' and aham che 'carved wood' (MS ahamche, divided as in the house table) are the words for the wooden people of the earlier parts. cautalic is not otherwise known; 'set up, arranged' follows Brasseur ('arrangés par ceux de Xibalba'), inferred, and the toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: Are cut nabe xqui quihila: “Cala, Huncame,” xeꜭha chire ri poy. “Cala, Vvcub Came,” xeꜭha chic chire ri aham che.
sentences.l: This then first they-greeted: “Hail, Huncame,” they-said to the effigy. “Hail, Vvcub Came,” they-said again to the carved wood.
sentences.i: These were the first they greeted: “Greetings, Huncame,” they said to the effigy. “Greetings, Vucub Came,” they said to the carved wooden figure.
sentences.n: A couplet, kept in one unit. quihila 'greet, pay honour to' is not otherwise known (Brasseur gihila, 'adorèrent'); inferred, toggle by the letters. Cala is a greeting; Brasseur's note says the word means 'clear, bright, open', a wish that all be clear for the one greeted, still used in the Verapaz. It may be the calah 'clear' of earlier parts (inferred); the toggle respells the letters (kala). The brothers take the figures for the two lords.

sentences.t: Ma cu xeꜭhacovic.
sentences.l: Not then they-answered.
sentences.i: But they gave no answer.
sentences.n: xeꜭhacovic 'they answered': xe- 'they' + ꜭhacov 'answer' + -ic (MS xeghacovic, a clear g, so ꜭh; Brasseur x-e chacouic). The root may be ꜭha 'speak' (inferred); toggle xech'akowik.

sentences.t: Catecut xe humuhub rahaual Xibalba chi ꜩe; xa que humin chic chi ꜩe conohel ahauab, rumal xe chacomahic chi qui ꜭux, xqui chac ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.l: Then they-roared(?) its-lords Xibalba with laughter; only they-roared(?) again with laughter all lords, because they-were-victors(?) in their heart, they-beat the Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.i: Then the lords of Xibalba burst out roaring with laughter; all the lords roared with laughter, because in their hearts they had already won: they had beaten Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu.
sentences.n: A couplet: xe humuhub … chi ꜩe, que humin … chi ꜩe 'they roared with laughter … they roared with laughter'. ꜩe 'laughter' (toggle tze', the modern word for laughing). humuhub and humin follow Brasseur ('burst out laughing', 'made a great noise of laughter'); humin is the huminic 'raise a tumult' of the last part (both guesses). chacomahic is read with Brasseur's note, 'they were victors in their hearts', from chac 'beat, win', as in xqui chac 'they had beaten' (inferred; the toggle keeps 009's chak). Brasseur's French turns xqui chac otherwise, 'qu'ils venaient de jouer', whom they had just tricked; 'beaten' follows his note on chacomahic (inferred). chi qui ꜭux 'in their hearts': the q-shaped letter is read ꜭ, as in the last part.

sentences.t: Xe ꜩeen na.
sentences.l: They-laughed still.
sentences.i: And they laughed and laughed.
sentences.n: ꜩeen 'laugh': ꜩe 'laughter' + -n, the verb; the doubled e marks the glottal stop (toggle tze'n, as caam is k'a'm). na 'still': they kept on laughing.

sentences.t: Catecut xeꜭhau chic Huncame, Vvcub Came: “Vꜩ bala, mix ix vlic.
sentences.l: Then they-spoke again Huncame, Vvcub Came: “Good bala, have-just you arrived.
sentences.i: Then Huncame and Vucub Came spoke: “Very well, you have come.
sentences.n: xeꜭhau 'they spoke': xe- + ꜭhau 'speak', as xꜭhau in ¶11. mix ix vlic 'you have just arrived': mi- 'just now' + x- completive, written mix as in earlier parts, then ix 'you (pl.)' and vlic 'arrive here'.

sentences.t: Chuvec chi caza vvach, ibate, ipachcab,” xe vꜭhax cut.
sentences.l: Tomorrow let caza(?) its-face, your-rings(?), your-hand-guards(?),” were-told then.
sentences.i: Tomorrow make ready your faces (?), your rings, your hand-guards,” they were told.
sentences.n: Chuvec 'tomorrow'. caza is not otherwise known. Brasseur reads ch'y qaza a vach and renders 'prepare your head ornaments, your rings, your gloves'; it may be ꜭaz 'live, wake', the caztah of ¶1 ('let our faces come alive'), as a play on that line (inferred). vvach is printed as written (Brasseur a vach 'your face'): v- 'its' does not fit beside ibate, ipachcab 'your rings, your hand-guards', with i- 'your (pl.)'. The English follows Brasseur's sense, a guess. The toggle gives uwach, as elsewhere, and kasa by the letters.

sentences.t: “Quix cu vloc chuvi ca tem,” xe vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: “You-come then hither on-top our bench,” they-were-told.
sentences.i: “Come up onto our bench,” they were told.
sentences.n: tem is taken here as 'bench, seat' (Brasseur 'our seat of honour'; tem is the modern word for a bench). In an earlier part the same letters were read 'holding' (uncertain). Quix … vloc 'come here, you (pl.)'.

sentences.t: Vtuquel cu catanalah abah qui tem.
sentences.l: Alone then burning-hot stone their bench.
sentences.i: But their bench was nothing but a burning-hot stone.
sentences.n: Vtuquel 'by itself, only'. catanalah 'burning hot': Brasseur qatanalah (his q is ꜭ), 'a red-hot stone'; taken as ꜭatan 'hot', the modern k'atan, + -alah, so the toggle restores k' (inferred). abah 'stone'. qui tem 'their bench', the lords'.

sentences.t: Xyaic, xe cat chicut chuvi tem;
sentences.l: It-was-given(?), they-burned again-then on-top bench;
sentences.i: They sat down on it (?), and they were burned on the bench;
sentences.n: Xyaic is not otherwise known: perhaps ya 'give, put' + -ic, 'it was done, they were set on it' (a guess; Brasseur 'sitting down on it'). xe cat 'they burned': cat 'burn' (Brasseur qat, his q is ꜭ; the modern k'at, the root of catanalah), so the toggle gives k'at, unlike cat 'you (one)'.

sentences.t: quiꜩih vi xe pizcalih chic chuvi tem, maui xe yacamaric; quiꜩih vi xe valehic, xcat qui culibal.
sentences.l: truly there they-writhed(?) again on-top bench, not they-were-eased(?); truly there they-rose-up(?), it-burned their seat(?).
sentences.i: they writhed on the bench indeed and found no relief; they sprang up indeed, burned where they sat.
sentences.n: The couplet quiꜩih vi xe …; quiꜩih vi xe … 'truly they …; truly they …'. pizcalih, yacamaric and valehic are read with Brasseur ('they rolled about on this throne without finding relief, and when they wanted to rise, the seat burned them'): pizcalih 'roll about, writhe' (guess); yacamaric perhaps from yac 'lift, raise', 'be eased' (guess; Brasseur's OCR has vacamaric); valehic 'rise up' (inferred). xcat qui culibal 'their culibal burned': culibal 'seat', a noun of place in -ibal (inferred). Toggle by the letters, but k'at as above.

sentences.t: Catecut xe ꜩeen chic Xibalba, xe pichicharic chi ꜩe;
sentences.l: Then they-laughed again Xibalba, they-pichicharic(?) with laughter;
sentences.i: Then Xibalba laughed again; they wept (?) with laughter;
sentences.n: xe ꜩeen 'they laughed', as in the last paragraph. pichicharic is not otherwise known; Brasseur renders 'they wept from laughing' (a guess; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: xvinaquiriheic vcumaꜩ ꜩe chi qui ꜭux, chi qui quiquib, chi qui baquib chi ꜩe conohel rahaual Xibalba.
sentences.l: it-came-into-being its-serpent laughter in their heart, in their blood, in their bone with laughter all its-lords Xibalba.
sentences.i: the serpent of laughter came alive in their hearts, in their blood, in their bones, all the lords of Xibalba, from laughing.
sentences.n: Brasseur says this verse is very hard to translate. xvinaquiriheic 'it came into being': vinaquir 'come into being', as in the first part, with an ending -iheic not otherwise known. vcumaꜩ ꜩe 'the serpent of laughter': cumaꜩ is the serpent of Ꜫucumaꜩ; perhaps a cramp or seizure of laughing (a guess; Brasseur 'they choked in their chests with laughter'). The three places: qui ꜭux 'their hearts', qui quiquib 'their blood' (quic + -ib, perhaps a plural; Brasseur quiqib; toggle kik'ib'), qui baquib 'their bones' (bac 'bone' + -ib; Brasseur bakib). The q-shaped letter of ꜭux is read ꜭ. In the manuscript a blotted letter stands between chi ꜩe and xvinaquiriheic (image 0038 line 10); nothing was read in it.

sentences.t: “Xa hix chi ha; ve chi be yaoc ichah, izic chi varabal,” xe vꜭhax cut.
sentences.l: “Only go-you to house; if(?) shall go to-be-given your-torch, your-cigar for sleeping,” were-told then.
sentences.i: “Just go to the house; your torch and your cigar will be brought to you there for the night,” they were told.
sentences.n: MS xahixchiha, vechibe yaoc ichah izic, divided by us. hix 'go, you (pl.)', of the 'go' verb of ho and he (Brasseur h'yx; toggle jix); ha 'house' (toggle ja). ve is left as 'if' in the literal line; Brasseur renders 'where'. chi be yaoc 'it shall go to be given': be 'go' + ya 'give' + -oc. ichah 'your (pl.) torch': chah is a splinter of resinous pine used as a torch (Brasseur's note; toggle chaj). izic 'your cigar' (Brasseur y ziq): zic is tobacco, a cigar (Brasseur's note, which also derives Spanish cigarro from it); toggle sik', with the k' of Brasseur's q and of the modern word (inferred). chi varabal 'for sleeping': var 'sleep' + -abal, as vvarabal 'its sleeping place'.

sentences.t: Catecut xe oponic pa Queꜫuma Ha; vtuquel queꜫum vpam chi ha.
sentences.l: Then they-arrived in Dark House; only darkness its-inside of house.
sentences.i: Then they came to the Dark House; inside the house there was nothing but darkness.
sentences.n: Queꜫuma Ha 'Dark House': queꜫum 'darkness' + -a, as the colour words take -a (ꜫana, queca), + ha 'house' (toggle Q'equma Ja). It is the first of the houses of trial in Xibalba; as a description it is translated (Brasseur 'la Maison Ténébreuse'). vpam 'its inside, its belly'. xe oponic 'they arrived there': opon + -ic, here kept before the place phrase pa Queꜫuma Ha.

sentences.t: Ta xqui cam cut qui naoh Xibalba:
sentences.l: Then they-took then their thought Xibalba:
sentences.i: Then Xibalba took counsel:
sentences.n: xqui cam qui naoh 'they took their thought', took counsel, as in the last part. The manuscript abbreviates the verb as xq̄cam (q with a stroke over it); it is expanded to xqui cam, as Brasseur has it.

sentences.t: “Xa que ca puzu chuvec; xa labe huzu huzu que camic, rumal vi queꜩabal ri ca chahibal,” que ꜭha curi Xibalba chi quibil quib.
sentences.l: “Only them we-sacrifice tomorrow; only labe(?) quickly quickly they-die, because indeed their-play-gear the our insult,” they-said then Xibalba among themselves.
sentences.i: “Let us just sacrifice them tomorrow; let them die quickly, quickly, for their game is an insult to us,” Xibalba said among themselves.
sentences.n: que ca puzu 'we sacrifice them': que, c- (ongoing) + e 'them', + ca- 'we' + puz, the word set beside naual in the first part, where its sense is uncertain and often connected with sacrifice, + -u (inferred; Brasseur 'let us sacrifice them'). labe is not explained (lab'e 'omen', uncertain, in earlier parts) and is left out of the English. huzu huzu 'quickly, quickly', toggled jusuk as in earlier parts. queꜩabal 'their gear for play', here their play itself. chahibal 'insult' (Brasseur 'affront, insult'): chah, which his note gives as 'wound, insult' among other senses, + -ibal (inferred). The same note says the passage plays on chah 'torch' and chaah 'ball game'.

sentences.t: Are curi qui chah xa coloquic cha, Zaquitoc v bi ri chah, v chah Xibalba;
sentences.l: This then their torch only round(?) flint(?), Zaquitoc its name the torch, its torch Xibalba;
sentences.i: Their torch was only a round flint (?), and Zaquitoc was the torch's name, the torch of Xibalba;
sentences.n: MS xacolo|quic cha. coloquic is taken as 'round' (Brasseur 'a round arrow'), a guess. cha is, in Brasseur's note, the word, the arrow, and the arrow point of obsidian or flint; here perhaps a flint point (guess). Zaquitoc (Brasseur zakitok) is kept as the name of the torch: zaqui 'white' + toc, which Brasseur takes as 'flint', 'white flint' (inferred).

sentences.t: xa hucul qui chaah, xa huzuc chi yohyox bac chicou vi ri qui chaah Xibalba.
sentences.l: only hucul(?) their game, only quickly yohyox(?) bone(?) chicou(?) there the their game Xibalba.
sentences.i: sharp (?) was their game, and quickly over (?): such was the game of Xibalba.
sentences.n: The least certain sentence of the part. hucul is a doubtful reading (the MS has u; Brasseur hakul), which Brasseur renders 'very sharp'; huzuc (MS u; Brasseur hazuk) is taken as 'quickly', as elsewhere (toggle jusuk). yohyox may be yoh 'undo, take apart' doubled, and bac 'bone'; chicou is not otherwise known. The English is a guess after Brasseur ('soon to reach its end, and so to encourage the game of Xibalba'). chaah 'game' plays on chah 'torch' (Brasseur's note at this sentence is on that play of cha, chah and chaah).

sentences.t: Xe oc cut ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu chupan ri Queꜫuma Ha.
sentences.l: They-entered then the Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu inside the Dark House.
sentences.i: So Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu went into the Dark House.
sentences.n: xe oc 'they entered' (oc 'enter'). chupan 'inside': chi + v- 'its' + pan, the pam of vpam above (toggle chupam).

sentences.t: Ta xbe cu yaoc qui chah, xa hun chi chah ꜩihom chic xel ruꜭ Huncame, Vvcub Came, ruꜭ huhun qui zic, xavi ꜩihon chic xel cuꜭ ahauab.
sentences.l: Then it-went then to-be-given their torch, only one of torch lit already it-came-out with Huncame, Vvcub Came, with each their cigar, also lit already it-came-out with-them lords.
sentences.i: Then their torch was brought in to them: a single torch, already lit, came from Huncame and Vucub Came, and with it each one's cigar, also lit, came from the lords.
sentences.n: A couplet: the torch from Huncame and Vucub Came, the cigars from the lords. xbe … yaoc 'it went to be given': be 'go' + ya 'give' + -oc. ꜩihom, ꜩihon 'lit': Brasseur 'allumée'; the same letters as ꜩih 'word' and the ꜩihon 'talk' of an earlier part, here taken as 'kindle, light' (inferred). xel ruꜭ 'it came out from beside him': ruꜭ 'with him', cuꜭ 'with them' (Brasseur's note: uꜭ 'with' comes four times here, three in this sentence and the cuꜭ of the next). huhun qui zic 'each one's cigar' (toggle sik', as izic in ¶15).

sentences.t: Ta xbe cu yaoc cuꜭ ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu, e chocochoh chi vloc pa queꜫum, ta xopon ri yaol qui chah ruꜭ qui zic.
sentences.l: When it-went then to-be-given with-them the Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu, they chocochoh(?) hither in darkness, when he-arrived the giver their torch with their cigar.
sentences.i: When the things were taken in to Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu, they were crouching (?) there in the dark when the bearer of their torch and their cigars arrived.
sentences.n: cuꜭ 'with them' here gives the persons the things were brought to. chocochoh is not otherwise known; Brasseur renders 'they were curled up on themselves in the dark' (a guess). chi vloc 'hither' is unexplained here. yaol 'giver, bearer': ya 'give' + -ol, the agent (the form of the last part's yaol, read there 'given'; inferred). queꜫum 'darkness'.

sentences.t: Cahulhut ri chah xoc apon oc.
sentences.l: Blazing(?) the torch it-entered arriving (oc).
sentences.i: The torch came in blazing (?).
sentences.n: Cahulhut is not otherwise known; Brasseur divides ca hulhut and renders 'the flame of the resin burst out at once as it came in' (a guess; toggle by the letters). xoc apon oc 'it entered, arriving there'.

sentences.t: Ri qui chah e qui ꜩiha ri huhun qui zic.
sentences.l: The their torch they they-light the each their cigar.
sentences.i: They were to light their torch, and each his cigar.
sentences.n: e qui ꜩiha (MS equiꜩiha; Brasseur e qui tziha) 'they light them': e 'they' + qui- 'they' + ꜩih 'light, kindle' + -a, the verb of ꜩihom above (inferred). Brasseur makes this the start of the lords' message, 'let each of them light his torch and his cigar', and it is read so here (inferred).

sentences.t: “He chul qui ya chi zaquiric, maui chi quizic; xavi xere v vach chul qui moloba,” que ꜭha ahauab chive, xe vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: “Go(?) come-here they-give at dawning, not that it-is-finished; just thus its face come-here they-gather(?),” they-say lords to-you, they-were-told.
sentences.i: “Let them come and give them back at dawn, not burned out; let them come and bring them back whole, just as they are, say the lords to you,” they were told.
sentences.n: A couplet: He chul qui ya … chul qui moloba 'let them come here and give … let them come here and gather (them)'. he is the 'go' of ¶1 (inferred; toggle je). chi zaquiric 'at dawn': the manuscript writes the z with a cedilla-like tail (çaquiric), as in 006 and 009; it is read z with Brasseur (zakiric). maui chi quizic 'that it be not finished' (MS chiquizic; Brasseur qiziq): quiz 'end, finish', the verb of the next sentence but one (toggle k'isik, as xquiz xk'is in earlier parts). xavi xere v vach 'just so its face', that is, whole, as given. moloba: mol 'gather' (inferred), 'bring back together'. que ꜭha ahauab chive 'say the lords to you (pl.)'.

sentences.t: Xe chacatah cut.
sentences.l: They-were-brought-low then.
sentences.i: So they were brought low.
sentences.n: Brasseur: 'thus they were defeated'. The torch and the cigar were the trial, and the brothers fail it.

sentences.t: Xqui quiz ri chah, xqui quiz curi zic, xha yao chique.
sentences.l: They-finished the torch, they-finished then cigar, xha(?) given to-them.
sentences.i: They used up the torch, they used up the cigar that had been given them.
sentences.n: A couplet: xqui quiz … xqui quiz 'they finished'. xha yao chique 'given to them': the letters are x h a, printed as written (Brasseur x-ha yao); xha is not explained, perhaps xa 'just' or a completive form (doubtful; toggle by the letters). yao 'give'; chique 'to them'.

sentences.t: Ꜩaꜩ curi vtihobal Xibalba, quia molah chi tihobal.
sentences.l: Many then its-trials Xibalba, many(?) heaps(?) of trials.
sentences.i: Many were the trials of Xibalba, trials of many kinds.
sentences.n: Ꜩaꜩ 'many, thick'. vtihobal 'its trials': tih 'try, test' + -obal, a place or means of trying (Brasseur tihobal 'trial'; his note sees in it the mysteries and initiation of Xibalba). In both words the t-i is a ligature that looks like ꜩh; read with Brasseur. quia molah (MS quia|molah, as Brasseur) 'many heaps (of)': quia 'many' and mol 'gather', both inferred (Brasseur 'of many different kinds'); the toggle respells the letters. The houses of trial are listed at the start of the next part.
